title: Color Gamuts in Botanical Illustration
content: Mervi Hjelmroos-Koski, Ph.D., D. Sc., Manager ofThe School of Botanical Art & Illustration in Denver, Colorado,recently gave her students an assignment to do a realistic botanical rendering as a way to understand color gamuts.Mervi says:"We recently completed an advanced level workshop which followedJames Gurney's bookColor and Light: A Guide for the Realist Painterfocusing on a botanical subject matter. The students learned aboutgamut mappingand limited palettes and found it to be extremely helpful in botanical work.""The class was very successful and several of the students even suggested that it should be a class within the required curriculum.""In the upper image no blue color was used - the lower image shows the same subject matter but without any yellow and blue added."Randy Raak was the instructor and the students used colored pencil.Please see more images from this course in addition to some other classroom shots by clickinghere.
